note: Files: iterate-runs abaybektursun-1115-{000503-1e5f,000525-ea4e,014823-ef56,014833-1daa} (hard328) and {000512-ee03,014843-85d9,000607-0e92,000621-1d7e} (MATH-500) answers.jsonl, fetched into runs/theory-tests/<job>/answers.jsonl. Each file has 1 row per problem, all with int score_v3, int n_new and gold; cap hits always come with finish_reason 'length'. Main reading, taken literally: C is cleaned in the stated order with a single strip at the start. After '$'/'*' are removed or \[ \( \] \) are cut, the whitespace left over is not stripped again. 'Strip a trailing .' removes one '.'. \boxed content is the last \boxed{ with its braces balanced; if it is unbalanced, the rest of the string is used. C is checked for being non-empty after cleaning. If 'Answer:' is present but only blank lines follow it, C = '' (no fallback to the last line). agree is called exactly as written, rln4_lib.agree(C, gold), which is n13_score.grade(C, gold): C goes in the gold slot of math_verify. That is asymmetric, so the swapped order could change a few rows. alt_measured: the same statistic with whitespace stripped again after every cleaning step. Bootstrap unit: (bench, problem_index), holding that problem's finished rows from up to 4 files. If a resample leaves a group empty, its value is 0.0 (unlikely). n = distinct problems in the smaller group (Short or Long). The groups line gives both row and problem counts. The 'fewer than 150' clause only means the number is reported anyway, so it does not change the output. example_row drops logprobs and prompt and truncates text.

Same 8 files, first-row rule, finished/wrong/candidate/cleaning/layout code and alt reading (whitespace stripped again after each cleaning step) as p1. M_L = median n_new of layout rows; M_F = median n_new of all finished rows with non-null n_new, layout rows included. An even count takes the mean of the two middle values. Bootstrap over (bench, problem_index) units; the ratio is recomputed per resample, and a resample with no layout rows gives 0.0. With few layout rows that 0.0 would pull the low end of the interval down. n = distinct problems among the layout rows (the smaller group). If there are no layout rows at all, the script prints not_computable (the recipe only covers fewer than 5). The same agree argument-order caveat as p1 applies.

Files: the 4 MATH-500 Think-SFT files only (000512-ee03, 014843-85d9, 000607-0e92, 000621-1d7e). Layout definition, cleaning and alt reading are as in p1. m = median n_new of the pooled finished rows. Low takes n_new <= m, High takes n_new > m, so ties at m go to Low. Bootstrap unit = problem_index (the problem's finished rows from up to 4 files). The median is recomputed inside each resample, which is the literal reading of 'compute m' as part of the statistic; holding m at its full-sample value would be the other choice for the interval only. n = distinct problems in the smaller of Low and High; problems can appear in both groups because samples differ in length. The groups line also prints m.
